key_insight: Finite element simulations show how thermally stressed NiTi–metal bilayer hinges can drive prescribed self-folding in microscale origami for biomedical implants.
engineering_relevance: Compact, self-deploying origami could support minimally invasive neurovascular implants that transform into tailored shapes after delivery.
method: Model thermal-expansion mismatch in NiTi paired with molybdenum or SS316L.
Optimize hinge length, layer thickness, width, and shape for controlled bending.
Integrate hinges into a waterbomb origami unit cell to evaluate coordinated folding.
evidence_signal: Simulations identified a hinge geometry enabling approximately 50% smaller unit-cell dimensions than previously reported designs and demonstrated coordinated folding in a complete unit cell.
watch_item: The abstract reports simulation results, not experimental validation of microscale fabrication or safe thermal actuation in vivo.
paper_title: Design of Self-Folding Origami Architectures for Biomedical Implants: A Finite Element Simulation Framework
